### Summary

Hey Streamlit team 👋,

I’m running into an odd issue on Streamlit Community Cloud with my app:
👉 https://global-t20-dash.streamlit.app/

The app used to run fine, but after some recent code updates, it now randomly crashes during startup. Sometimes it loads fully and works for several minutes, and sometimes (even without any new changes) it instantly shows:

Oh no. Error running app.
If this keeps happening, please contact support.

There’s no traceback visible in the UI, and the app page doesn’t show any specific error.
In the deployment logs I occasionally see:

The service has encountered an error while checking the health of the Streamlit app:
Get "http://localhost:8501/script-health-check": EOF

It looks like the app sometimes fails the health check and gets killed.

What I'm seeing

App works on some runs, crashes on others.
Behavior changes even without modifying code.
No Python error is printed — only the “Oh no. Error running app” message.
The crash happens before the UI fully loads.
Restarting the app or refreshing sometimes fixes it temporarily.
What the app does

Loads Parquet files (cached using @st.cache_data)
Generates multiple Plotly charts
Uses forms + filters + session state
No long-running background tasks
Steps to reproduce

Open the app link: https://global-t20-dash.streamlit.app/
Sometimes it loads successfully.
Refresh the page a few times.
Eventually it shows the error screen (“Oh no. Error running app”).
Expected behavior

The app should load consistently without crashing during startup.

Actual behavior

Startup is unreliable & sometimes it works, sometimes it dies with the health-check EOF error.

Streamlit Community Cloud

initial_report:
cache_data failing to serialize classes from v1.44.0

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I noticed in the upgrade from 1.43.0 to 1.44.0 that we are getting UnserializableReturnValueError when calling cache_data with a self defined class. I can confirm pickle dumps and loads works fine for this class when I run it outside of streamlit. 

Full error:
> streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type __main__.Example) in test(). st.cache_data uses pickle to serialize the function's return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see our docs for differences).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit import cache_data
import datetime as dt

class Example:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

@cache_data(ttl=dt.timedelta(minutes=60))
def test():
    name = "andy"
    return Example(name)

if __name__ == '__main__':

    b = test()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the code above in streamlit

### Expected Behavior

The class should be pickled and be stored in the cache

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.44.0
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: شاید تابع بازگردانده شده به صورت مستقیم یک کلاس تعریف شده خودکار باشد که streamlit قادر به سریالی‌سازی آن نیست.

Incomplete type hint for date_input max_value: missing Literal["today"]

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi,

It looks like the type hints for `st.date_input` are incomplete.

In `time_widgets.date_input`, the `max_value` parameter is typed as `SingleDateValue`, but the function also accepts the string literal `"today"`, as documented and supported at runtime.

This causes static type checkers (e.g. mypy, pyright, pylance) to raise errors even though the code is valid.

Suggested fix:
Extend the type hint to include Literal["today"]
This likely affects min_value as well.

Thanks!

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.date_input(
    "Select a date",
    max_value="today",
)
```

### Summary

Watch discuss Topic:
https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/after-upload-file-stays-in-ram/119453/2

Streamlit Version 1.49.1
Python Version 3.13.7

I searched for the issue on all known databases without success

I am facing the following issue with st.file_uploader:

When I am uploading a File about 600MB the RAM usage is after I selected the File about 660 MB.
At the moment I pressed the upload button the RAM usage increases up to 1800MB.
After the Upload is done, the RAM usage stays at 660MB.
If I close the browsertab it stays at 660MB, only when I close the streamlit instance the RAM gets free.

I tryed several solutions:

clear_on_submit=True
working with session state keys
gc.collect()
st.rerun()

The phenomenon is:
If I set the clear_on_submit=false and deactivate the st.rerun() I am able to delete the File in the Widget and only then the file gets deleted from the RAM.

I tested it with a simple Upload code with the same result in different browsers on 2 different PCs and different streamlit versions.

Actually I have no idea how to fix this, can somebody help?

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
-------- Upload-Helper --------

def save_uploaded_file(file, folder):
os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
save_path = os.path.join(folder, file.name)

with open(save_path, "wb") as f:
    shutil.copyfileobj(file, f)

return save_path
def unified_upload(device_id):
st.subheader(“:open_file_folder: Dokument hochladen”)

# Dokumenttypen + erlaubte Dateiendungen
doc_types = {
    "Firmware": {"label": "💾 Firmware", "allowed_types": ["zip", "pdf"]},
    "Manual": {"label": "📘 Servicemanual", "allowed_types": ["pdf"]},
    "Partslist": {"label": "🛠️ Partslist", "allowed_types": ["pdf"]},
    "Bulletin": {"label": "📑 Bulletin", "allowed_types": ["pdf"]},
}

# Upload-Counter initialisieren
if "upload_counter" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.upload_counter = {}

if device_id not in st.session_state.upload_counter:
    st.session_state.upload_counter[device_id] = 0

# Dropdown zur Auswahl des Dokumententyps
doc_choice = st.selectbox(
    "Dokumenttyp auswählen",
    options=list(doc_types.keys()),
    format_func=lambda x: doc_types[x]["label"],
    index=None,
    placeholder="Bitte auswählen...",
    key=f"doc_select_{device_id}"
)

if not doc_choice:
    st.info("Bitte zuerst den Dokumenttyp auswählen ⬆️")
    return

# Zielordner für Gerät & Typ
folder = os.path.join(r"D:\ServiceInfoToolData", str(device_id), doc_choice)
os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)

# Dynamischen Key für file_uploader
file_key = f"file_upload_{device_id}_{doc_choice}_{st.session_state.upload_counter[device_id]}"

# Upload-Formular mit Auto-Reset
with st.form(f"upload_form_{device_id}_{doc_choice}", clear_on_submit=True):
    file = st.file_uploader(
        f"{doc_types[doc_choice]['label']} hochladen",
        type=doc_types[doc_choice]["allowed_types"],
        key=file_key
    )

    title = st.text_input("Titel (optional)")
    submitted = st.form_submit_button("Speichern")

    if submitted:
        if file is None:
            st.error("Bitte eine Datei auswählen.")
        else:
            save_path = save_uploaded_file(file, folder)

            # DB-Eintrag speichern
            conn = get_connection()
            try:
                conn.execute(
                    """
                    INSERT INTO serviceinfos 
                    (geraet_id, typ, dateiname, pfad, uploaded_at, version) 
                    VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)
                    """,
                    (
                        device_id,
                        doc_choice,
                        file.name,
                        save_path,
                        datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                        title.strip() or None,
                    ),
                )
                conn.commit()
            finally:
                conn.close()

            # Upload-Counter hochzählen, damit nächster Upload einen neuen Key bekommt
            st.session_state.upload_counter[device_id] += 1

            # Speicher freigeben
            del file
            st.session_state._uploaded_file_mgr = UploadedFileManager()
            gc.collect()
            st.rerun()

            st.success(f"{doc_types[doc_choice]['label']} hochgeladen ✅")
```

```python
# comp.py

import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import streamlit as st

st_comp_get_cookies = st.components.v2.component(
    "component_bidi_drop_bug.get_cookies",
    js="""
    export default function(component){
        const { data, setTriggerValue } = component;
        console.log("Comp Instantiated: " + data._);
        // More advanced logic here
        const retObj = document.cookie;
        console.log("cookie-getter:", retObj);
        if(retObj !== undefined) setTriggerValue("get_cookies", retObj);
    }
    """,
    isolate_styles=False,
)

def _frame_gen(frame, skip=0):
    while frame:
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"
```

streamlit v 1.55

I'm trying to migrate our custom js widgets from v1 component api to the non-iframe v2 api.
It seems far more powerful, and seems like it'll cut boilerplate.
In our style, we have accumulated over the years a collection of js/client side running code, that doesn't particularly need/have an html or user-interfacing component.

I think I've noticed an issue, where values are getting returned from the js frontend (as seen by console.log msgs), but the streamlit backend logs see those msgs as dropped. I'm still getting the hang of the runtime behaviors of this new component api, to figure out how to update our v1 components, so I've been trying to test it. If this is not the expected or correct usage, I'm all ears, but I'm working my best from the online docs + repo src implementation. 

This is our current design / usage analysis of the v2 api:
- We declare/write a st.components.v2.component(...) object in a helper file, that will not be modified, with a unique name
- The js string includes all helper functions, and an `export default function(component: FrontendRendererArgs)`
- This default function is the per-widget-instantiation, and only run once (see below)
- It sets up callbacks or such on html elements
- If the component is called with a `key`, then all setTriggerValue and setStateValue items populate session_state
- Without an explicit `key`, setTriggerValue won't populate session_state, but the rest of the python arguments (data) are used to calculate a unique frontend key
- No two component instances therefore can have the exact same args (data)
- If the args to the component don't change, the widget object stays created, and is not re-instantiated
- If the rest of the args (data) to the component change, without a `key`, the old widget is discarded, and a new component is instantiated

Our goal is to have high-level code that uses caching & post processing of raw lower-level data call these low-level components as needed. But if the components are called, I expect them to behave consistently. 

In this particular example, the js component does (for example!!!) a failproof cookies query on instantiation and returns it via setTriggerValue.
```js
export default function (component){  component.setTriggerValue("get_cookies", document.cookie); }
```
We wrap that `st_comp_get_cookies: st.components.v2.component` in a helper function.
```python
def get_raw_cookies():
    obj = st_comp_get_cookies(data={"_": unique_line_time()})
```
If we feed `data` a value that's unique to the line (line traceback stack), the multiple calls of the widget will be unique even if fed the same other args. It would create a new component when there's a new/unique call (args or location), otherwise only instantiated once.
If we feed `data` a value that's unique in time, then every call is a new widget instance, and the js default function runs each time.

In the v1 api, when the app first loaded, the components wouldn't always respond right away. So I'd check if the returned value was empty or not.
```python
# get_raw_cookies()
if not isisntance(obj, dict) or "get_cookies" not in obj:
    # Very first run, component mightn't be ready
    time.sleep(initial_setup_sleep)
    st.rerun()
print(f"{obj["get_cookies"]=}")
```

Given the above files, with more logging added, I noticed a very strange behavior. (This is just a heavily reduced version of our real prod code; and I only chose documents.cookies because it _can't fail_).
In the browser console, everytime the page reloaded (hard reload F5, or soft rerun from some other input), the console logged the new widget instance, the cookie fetch, and that succeeded.
But in the python logs, sometimes it worked, sometimes it did not. 
With the "rerun if fail" check, if this was the only indeterminite execution, it'd work quickly enough, and then the rest of the code would execute.
But with multiple components doing this, it suddenly became impossible for both to work at the same time.
```python
get_raw_cookies() # Sometimes reruns, ok
get_raw_cookies() # Always reruns, when the above finally works
st.header("This never runs")
assert False
```

Sorry if this was rather long winded, but I'm either uncertain I'm understanding the runtime behaviors correctly, trying not to misrepresent our goals, possibly oblivious to a better v2 design, or just unaware of what to reasonably expect from this as for behavior.

### Expected Behavior

I expect at app start the component to fail, but afterwards I'd expect each new component creation to successfully be created, successfully transmit setState/TriggerValue back to the component, and get returned by the component, before the backend continues on. (Consistency / Determinism). (Otherwise, we'd design differently)

### Current Behavior

I've tried variations of the above files, such as adding more sleeps on python side, but the js side seems to be sending the values back, and the python side seems to inconsistently receive them. The first component ~1/2 the time, and the second always fails when the first doesn't.

### Summary

Hi,

It looks like the type hints for `st.date_input` are incomplete.

In `time_widgets.date_input`, the `max_value` parameter is typed as `SingleDateValue`, but the function also accepts the string literal `"today"`, as documented and supported at runtime.

This causes static type checkers (e.g. mypy, pyright, pylance) to raise errors even though the code is valid.

Suggested fix:
Extend the type hint to include Literal["today"]
This likely affects min_value as well.

Thanks!

I'm trying to migrate our custom js widgets from v1 component api to the non-iframe v2 api.
It seems far more powerful, and seems like it'll cut boilerplate.
In our style, we have accumulated over the years a collection of js/client side running code, that doesn't particularly need/have an html or user-interfacing component.

I think I've noticed an issue, where values are getting returned from the js frontend (as seen by console.log msgs), but the streamlit backend logs see those msgs as dropped. I'm still getting the hang of the runtime behaviors of this new component api, to figure out how to update our v1 components, so I've been trying to test it. If this is not the expected or correct usage, I'm all ears, but I'm working my best from the online docs + repo src implementation. 

This is our current design / usage analysis of the v2 api:
- We declare/write a st.components.v2.component(...) object in a helper file, that will not be modified, with a unique name
- The js string includes all helper functions, and an `export default function(component: FrontendRendererArgs)`
- This default function is the per-widget-instantiation, and only run once (see below)
- It sets up callbacks or such on html elements
- If the component is called with a `key`, then all setTriggerValue and setStateValue items populate session_state
- Without an explicit `key`, setTriggerValue won't populate session_state, but the rest of the python arguments (data) are used to calculate a unique frontend key
- No two component instances therefore can have the exact same args (data)
- If the args to the component don't change, the widget object stays created, and is not re-instantiated
- If the rest of the args (data) to the component change, without a `key`, the old widget is discarded, and a new component is instantiated

Our goal is to have high-level code that uses caching & post processing of raw lower-level data call these low-level components as needed. But if the components are called, I expect them to behave consistently. 

In this particular example, the js component does (for example!!!) a failproof cookies query on instantiation and returns it via setTriggerValue.
```js
export default function (component){  component.setTriggerValue("get_cookies", document.cookie); }
```
We wrap that `st_comp_get_cookies: st.components.v2.component` in a helper function.
```python
def get_raw_cookies():
    obj = st_comp_get_cookies(data={"_": unique_line_time()})
```
If we feed `data` a value that's unique to the line (line traceback stack), the multiple calls of the widget will be unique even if fed the same other args. It would create a new component when there's a new/unique call (args or location), otherwise only instantiated once.
If we feed `data` a value that's unique in time, then every call is a new widget instance, and the js default function runs each time.

In the v1 api, when the app first loaded, the components wouldn't always respond right away. So I'd check if the returned value was empty or not.
```python
# get_raw_cookies()
if not isisntance(obj, dict) or "get_cookies" not in obj:
    # Very first run, component mightn't be ready
    time.sleep(initial_setup_sleep)
    st.rerun()
print(f"{obj["get_cookies"]=}")
```

Given the above files, with more logging added, I noticed a very strange behavior. (This is just a heavily reduced version of our real prod code; and I only chose documents.cookies because it _can't fail_).
In the browser console, everytime the page reloaded (hard reload F5, or soft rerun from some other input), the console logged the new widget instance, the cookie fetch, and that succeeded.
But in the python logs, sometimes it worked, sometimes it did not. 
With the "rerun if fail" check, if this was the only indeterminite execution, it'd work quickly enough, and then the rest of the code would execute.
But with multiple components doing this, it suddenly became impossible for both to work at the same time.
```python
get_raw_cookies() # Sometimes reruns, ok
get_raw_cookies() # Always reruns, when the above finally works
st.header("This never runs")
assert False
```

Sorry if this was rather long winded, but I'm either uncertain I'm understanding the runtime behaviors correctly, trying not to misrepresent our goals, possibly oblivious to a better v2 design, or just unaware of what to reasonably expect from this as for behavior.

### Expected Behavior

I expect at app start the component to fail, but afterwards I'd expect each new component creation to successfully be created, successfully transmit setState/TriggerValue back to the component, and get returned by the component, before the backend continues on. ### Current Behavior

I've tried variations of the above files, such as adding more sleeps on python side, but the js side seems to be sending the values back, and the python side seems to inconsistently receive them. The first component ~1/2 the time, and the second always fails when the first doesn't.

```text
When you upload a file using [`st.file_uploader`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader), the data are copied to the Streamlit backend via the browser, and contained in a BytesIO buffer in Python memory (i.e. RAM, not disk). The data will persist in RAM until the Streamlit app re-runs from top-to-bottom, which is on each widget interaction. If you need to save the data that was uploaded between runs, then you can [cache](/develop/concepts/architecture/caching) it so that Streamlit persists it across re-runs.
```

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: ممکن است فایل آپلود شده پس از ارسال پاک نشود به دلیل نحوه مدیریت حافظه استریم‌لیت باشد.

initial_report:
st.tabs switches back to the first tab if an element is added or removed before the tabs

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Tabs should (and usually do) save their state between reruns so that if I adjust a widget inside a tab, that same tab stays visible.
However, if the rerun adds/removes a widget _above_ the tabs' declaration, the tab state is reset to the first tab no matter which tab was visible when the above-the-tabs widget was added/removed.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

if "enabled" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled:
    st.button("Hi there!")

a, b = st.tabs(["Tab 1", "Tab 2"])

if "enabled_safe" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled_safe:
    st.button("Phew, safe!")

with a:
    st.write("Hello, world!")

with b:
    message = """Toggling the first switch will cause a button to
appear or disappear above the tabs. This causes the tabs to
reset to the first tab, incorrectly, in my opinion.

Toggling the second (safe) switch causes the button to appear
or disappear below the tabs, which preserves the tab state (correctly)."""
    st.write(message)
    enabled = st.toggle("Display it!", key="enabled")
    enabled_safe = st.toggle("This one's safe", key="enabled_safe")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch the provided code example
2. Open Tab 2 to reveal the toggles
3. Toggle the "Display it!" switch which will cause a new button to appear above the tabs
4. The tab will reset to Tab 1

I have experimented with a few different setups and it appears only adding/removing widgets causes this issue.
Simply changing the state of a widget (e.g. the label of a button) does not cause this issue.

### Expected Behavior

I expect that having a new button or other widget appear above a set of tabs
would not change which tab is currently visible.

### Current Behavior

See steps to reproduce.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3a172ba-92e2-4ec7-bcea-6d1ec0fde7b9

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.52.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Debian 3.12 Trixie (Docker)
- Browser: Brave (Chrome) (Brave 1.83.118 / Chromium: 141.0.7390.108)


### Additional Information

I believe this is the same issue as #11160 but that issue author never responded.

initial_report:
st.cache_data on class methods intermittently raises UnserializableReturnValueError

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'X'>: it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
### `repro_model.py`


"""Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file."""

class MyResult:
    def __init__(self, output: str = "", value: int = 0):
        self.output = output
        self.value = value


### `repro_agent.py`


"""
Helper module imported once by repro.py.
Simulates agents/__init__.py — only loaded once, holds a stale class reference
after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher.
"""
import streamlit as st
from repro_model import MyResult  # bound once at import time


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    import time
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return MyResult(output=f"result for {key}", value=42)


### `repro.py` — run with `streamlit run repro.py`


import streamlit as st
import sys
import importlib
import repro_agent  # imported once — simulates agents/__init__.py


st.title("cache_data pickle race condition repro")

if st.button("1) Normal call (works)"):
    try:
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")

if st.button("2) Simulate file-watcher then call (fails, and keeps failing)"):
    # This is exactly what LocalSourcesWatcher.on_path_changed does:
    #   for wm in self._watched_modules.values():
    #       del sys.modules[wm.module_name]
    if "repro_model" in sys.modules:
        del sys.modules["repro_model"]

    # Re-import creates a NEW class object in sys.modules
    importlib.import_module("repro_model")

    # Clear cache so pickle.dumps is attempted again
    repro_agent.get_result.clear()

    try:
        # repro_agent still uses the OLD MyResult class.
        # pickle resolves sys.modules["repro_model"].MyResult → NEW class.
        # OLD is not NEW → PicklingError → UnserializableReturnValueError
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

**Steps:**
1. `streamlit run repro.py`
2. Click **"1) Normal call"** — succeeds.
3. Click **"2) Simulate file-watcher"** — fails with `UnserializableReturnValueError`.
4. Click **"1) Normal call"** again — **also fails**, until Streamlit is restarted.


### Expected Behavior

Step 4 demonstrates persistence: `repro_agent` is never re-imported, so it keeps
using the old class, while `sys.modules` keeps the new one.

Neither step 3 not step 4 should throw the `UnserializableReturnValueError`.

Expected behavior : 

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Current Behavior

`UnserializableReturnValueError` is thrown

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- **Streamlit**: 1.55.0
- **Python**: 3.13.7
- **OS**: Windows 11 / Linux (Kubernetes)
- Occurs more frequently in local dev (active filesystem) than in deployed containers

### Additional Information

> **Disclosure**: This bug report was written by an LLM (Claude) after a deep investigation into a production issue. The root cause analysis, reproduction script, and identified problematic code path are all LLM-generated

## Suggested Fixes

### Option A: Chain the original exception (low-effort, improves DX)

In `_handle_cache_miss`, chain the original exception so users can see the real error:

```python
raise UnserializableReturnValueError(
    return_value=computed_value, func=self._info.func
) from ex  # <-- add "from ex"
```

### Option B: Guard `write_result` against stale class references

Before calling `pickle.dumps()` in `DataCache.write_result`, re-import the module and verify class identity:

```python
import importlib
cls = type(value)
mod = sys.modules.get(cls.__module__)
if mod is not None:
    current_cls = getattr(mod, cls.__qualname__, None)
    if current_cls is not None and current_cls is not cls:
        # Module was reloaded — update the instance's class to the current one
        value.__class__ = current_cls
```

### Option C: Don't delete modules from `sys.modules` preemptively

Instead of deleting all watched modules on every file change, only invalidate the module that actually changed. Or defer the deletion to the start of the next script run rather than doing it immediately from the watcher thread.

## Workaround

Return only pickle-safe primitives (dicts, strings, numbers) from `@st.cache_data` functions, and reconstruct custom objects outside the cache boundary:

```python
@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def _cached_call(key: str) -> dict:
    result = do_expensive_work(key)
    return result.__dict__  # dict is always pickle-safe

def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    return MyResult(**_cached_call(key))
```

### Summary

I noticed in the upgrade from 1.43.0 to 1.44.0 that we are getting UnserializableReturnValueError when calling cache_data with a self defined class. I can confirm pickle dumps and loads works fine for this class when I run it outside of streamlit. 

Full error:
> streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type __main__.Example) in test(). st.cache_data uses pickle to serialize the function's return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see our docs for differences).

```Python
from streamlit import cache_data
import datetime as dt

class Example:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

@cache_data(ttl=dt.timedelta(minutes=60))
def test():
    name = "andy"
    return Example(name)

if __name__ == '__main__':

    b = test()
```

```python
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"
```

I'm trying to migrate our custom js widgets from v1 component api to the non-iframe v2 api.
It seems far more powerful, and seems like it'll cut boilerplate.
In our style, we have accumulated over the years a collection of js/client side running code, that doesn't particularly need/have an html or user-interfacing component.

I think I've noticed an issue, where values are getting returned from the js frontend (as seen by console.log msgs), but the streamlit backend logs see those msgs as dropped. I'm still getting the hang of the runtime behaviors of this new component api, to figure out how to update our v1 components, so I've been trying to test it. If this is not the expected or correct usage, I'm all ears, but I'm working my best from the online docs + repo src implementation. 

This is our current design / usage analysis of the v2 api:
- We declare/write a st.components.v2.component(...) object in a helper file, that will not be modified, with a unique name
- The js string includes all helper functions, and an `export default function(component: FrontendRendererArgs)`
- This default function is the per-widget-instantiation, and only run once (see below)
- It sets up callbacks or such on html elements
- If the component is called with a `key`, then all setTriggerValue and setStateValue items populate session_state
- Without an explicit `key`, setTriggerValue won't populate session_state, but the rest of the python arguments (data) are used to calculate a unique frontend key
- No two component instances therefore can have the exact same args (data)
- If the args to the component don't change, the widget object stays created, and is not re-instantiated
- If the rest of the args (data) to the component change, without a `key`, the old widget is discarded, and a new component is instantiated

Our goal is to have high-level code that uses caching & post processing of raw lower-level data call these low-level components as needed. But if the components are called, I expect them to behave consistently. 

In this particular example, the js component does (for example!!!) a failproof cookies query on instantiation and returns it via setTriggerValue.
```js
export default function (component){  component.setTriggerValue("get_cookies", document.cookie); }
```
We wrap that `st_comp_get_cookies: st.components.v2.component` in a helper function.
```python
def get_raw_cookies():
    obj = st_comp_get_cookies(data={"_": unique_line_time()})
```
If we feed `data` a value that's unique to the line (line traceback stack), the multiple calls of the widget will be unique even if fed the same other args. It would create a new component when there's a new/unique call (args or location), otherwise only instantiated once.
If we feed `data` a value that's unique in time, then every call is a new widget instance, and the js default function runs each time.

In the v1 api, when the app first loaded, the components wouldn't always respond right away. So I'd check if the returned value was empty or not.
```python
# get_raw_cookies()
if not isisntance(obj, dict) or "get_cookies" not in obj:
    # Very first run, component mightn't be ready
    time.sleep(initial_setup_sleep)
    st.rerun()
print(f"{obj["get_cookies"]=}")
```

Given the above files, with more logging added, I noticed a very strange behavior. (This is just a heavily reduced version of our real prod code; and I only chose documents.cookies because it _can't fail_).
In the browser console, everytime the page reloaded (hard reload F5, or soft rerun from some other input), the console logged the new widget instance, the cookie fetch, and that succeeded.
But in the python logs, sometimes it worked, sometimes it did not. 
With the "rerun if fail" check, if this was the only indeterminite execution, it'd work quickly enough, and then the rest of the code would execute.
But with multiple components doing this, it suddenly became impossible for both to work at the same time.
```python
get_raw_cookies() # Sometimes reruns, ok
get_raw_cookies() # Always reruns, when the above finally works
st.header("This never runs")
assert False
```

Sorry if this was rather long winded, but I'm either uncertain I'm understanding the runtime behaviors correctly, trying not to misrepresent our goals, possibly oblivious to a better v2 design, or just unaware of what to reasonably expect from this as for behavior.

initial_report:
st.cache_data on class methods intermittently raises UnserializableReturnValueError

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'X'>: it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
### `repro_model.py`


"""Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file."""

class MyResult:
    def __init__(self, output: str = "", value: int = 0):
        self.output = output
        self.value = value


### `repro_agent.py`


"""
Helper module imported once by repro.py.
Simulates agents/__init__.py — only loaded once, holds a stale class reference
after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher.
"""
import streamlit as st
from repro_model import MyResult  # bound once at import time


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    import time
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return MyResult(output=f"result for {key}", value=42)


### `repro.py` — run with `streamlit run repro.py`


import streamlit as st
import sys
import importlib
import repro_agent  # imported once — simulates agents/__init__.py


st.title("cache_data pickle race condition repro")

if st.button("1) Normal call (works)"):
    try:
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")

if st.button("2) Simulate file-watcher then call (fails, and keeps failing)"):
    # This is exactly what LocalSourcesWatcher.on_path_changed does:
    #   for wm in self._watched_modules.values():
    #       del sys.modules[wm.module_name]
    if "repro_model" in sys.modules:
        del sys.modules["repro_model"]

    # Re-import creates a NEW class object in sys.modules
    importlib.import_module("repro_model")

    # Clear cache so pickle.dumps is attempted again
    repro_agent.get_result.clear()

    try:
        # repro_agent still uses the OLD MyResult class.
        # pickle resolves sys.modules["repro_model"].MyResult → NEW class.
        # OLD is not NEW → PicklingError → UnserializableReturnValueError
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

**Steps:**
1. `streamlit run repro.py`
2. Click **"1) Normal call"** — succeeds.
3. Click **"2) Simulate file-watcher"** — fails with `UnserializableReturnValueError`.
4. Click **"1) Normal call"** again — **also fails**, until Streamlit is restarted.


### Expected Behavior

Step 4 demonstrates persistence: `repro_agent` is never re-imported, so it keeps
using the old class, while `sys.modules` keeps the new one.

Neither step 3 not step 4 should throw the `UnserializableReturnValueError`.

Expected behavior : 

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Current Behavior

`UnserializableReturnValueError` is thrown

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- **Streamlit**: 1.55.0
- **Python**: 3.13.7
- **OS**: Windows 11 / Linux (Kubernetes)
- Occurs more frequently in local dev (active filesystem) than in deployed containers

### Additional Information

> **Disclosure**: This bug report was written by an LLM (Claude) after a deep investigation into a production issue. The root cause analysis, reproduction script, and identified problematic code path are all LLM-generated

## Suggested Fixes

### Option A: Chain the original exception (low-effort, improves DX)

In `_handle_cache_miss`, chain the original exception so users can see the real error:

```python
raise UnserializableReturnValueError(
    return_value=computed_value, func=self._info.func
) from ex  # <-- add "from ex"
```

### Option B: Guard `write_result` against stale class references

Before calling `pickle.dumps()` in `DataCache.write_result`, re-import the module and verify class identity:

```python
import importlib
cls = type(value)
mod = sys.modules.get(cls.__module__)
if mod is not None:
    current_cls = getattr(mod, cls.__qualname__, None)
    if current_cls is not None and current_cls is not cls:
        # Module was reloaded — update the instance's class to the current one
        value.__class__ = current_cls
```

### Option C: Don't delete modules from `sys.modules` preemptively

Instead of deleting all watched modules on every file change, only invalidate the module that actually changed. Or defer the deletion to the start of the next script run rather than doing it immediately from the watcher thread.

## Workaround

Return only pickle-safe primitives (dicts, strings, numbers) from `@st.cache_data` functions, and reconstruct custom objects outside the cache boundary:

```python
@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def _cached_call(key: str) -> dict:
    result = do_expensive_work(key)
    return result.__dict__  # dict is always pickle-safe

def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    return MyResult(**_cached_call(key))
```

initial_report:
st.cache_data on class methods intermittently raises UnserializableReturnValueError

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'X'>: it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
### `repro_model.py`


"""Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file."""

class MyResult:
    def __init__(self, output: str = "", value: int = 0):
        self.output = output
        self.value = value


### `repro_agent.py`


"""
Helper module imported once by repro.py.
Simulates agents/__init__.py — only loaded once, holds a stale class reference
after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher.
"""
import streamlit as st
from repro_model import MyResult  # bound once at import time


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    import time
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return MyResult(output=f"result for {key}", value=42)


### `repro.py` — run with `streamlit run repro.py`


import streamlit as st
import sys
import importlib
import repro_agent  # imported once — simulates agents/__init__.py


st.title("cache_data pickle race condition repro")

if st.button("1) Normal call (works)"):
    try:
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")

if st.button("2) Simulate file-watcher then call (fails, and keeps failing)"):
    # This is exactly what LocalSourcesWatcher.on_path_changed does:
    #   for wm in self._watched_modules.values():
    #       del sys.modules[wm.module_name]
    if "repro_model" in sys.modules:
        del sys.modules["repro_model"]

    # Re-import creates a NEW class object in sys.modules
    importlib.import_module("repro_model")

    # Clear cache so pickle.dumps is attempted again
    repro_agent.get_result.clear()

    try:
        # repro_agent still uses the OLD MyResult class.
        # pickle resolves sys.modules["repro_model"].MyResult → NEW class.
        # OLD is not NEW → PicklingError → UnserializableReturnValueError
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

**Steps:**
1. `streamlit run repro.py`
2. Click **"1) Normal call"** — succeeds.
3. Click **"2) Simulate file-watcher"** — fails with `UnserializableReturnValueError`.
4. Click **"1) Normal call"** again — **also fails**, until Streamlit is restarted.


### Expected Behavior

Step 4 demonstrates persistence: `repro_agent` is never re-imported, so it keeps
using the old class, while `sys.modules` keeps the new one.

Neither step 3 not step 4 should throw the `UnserializableReturnValueError`.

Expected behavior : 

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Current Behavior

`UnserializableReturnValueError` is thrown

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- **Streamlit**: 1.55.0
- **Python**: 3.13.7
- **OS**: Windows 11 / Linux (Kubernetes)
- Occurs more frequently in local dev (active filesystem) than in deployed containers

### Additional Information

> **Disclosure**: This bug report was written by an LLM (Claude) after a deep investigation into a production issue. The root cause analysis, reproduction script, and identified problematic code path are all LLM-generated

## Suggested Fixes

### Option A: Chain the original exception (low-effort, improves DX)

In `_handle_cache_miss`, chain the original exception so users can see the real error:

```python
raise UnserializableReturnValueError(
    return_value=computed_value, func=self._info.func
) from ex  # <-- add "from ex"
```

### Option B: Guard `write_result` against stale class references

Before calling `pickle.dumps()` in `DataCache.write_result`, re-import the module and verify class identity:

```python
import importlib
cls = type(value)
mod = sys.modules.get(cls.__module__)
if mod is not None:
    current_cls = getattr(mod, cls.__qualname__, None)
    if current_cls is not None and current_cls is not cls:
        # Module was reloaded — update the instance's class to the current one
        value.__class__ = current_cls
```

### Option C: Don't delete modules from `sys.modules` preemptively

Instead of deleting all watched modules on every file change, only invalidate the module that actually changed. Or defer the deletion to the start of the next script run rather than doing it immediately from the watcher thread.

## Workaround

Return only pickle-safe primitives (dicts, strings, numbers) from `@st.cache_data` functions, and reconstruct custom objects outside the cache boundary:

```python
@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def _cached_call(key: str) -> dict:
    result = do_expensive_work(key)
    return result.__dict__  # dict is always pickle-safe

def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    return MyResult(**_cached_call(key))
```

شاهد مستند: متن رسمی؛ سازگاری نسخه باید بررسی شود.

بخش منبع:

```text
Where does st.file_uploader store uploaded files and when do they get deleted?
```

نسخهٔ منبع:

```text
695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd
```

متن شاهد:

```text
When you upload a file using [`st.file_uploader`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader), the data are copied to the Streamlit backend via the browser, and contained in a BytesIO buffer in Python memory (i.e. RAM, not disk). The data will persist in RAM until the Streamlit app re-runs from top-to-bottom, which is on each widget interaction. If you need to save the data that was uploaded between runs, then you can [cache](/develop/concepts/architecture/caching) it so that Streamlit persists it across re-runs.
```

نشانی منبع:

```text
https://github.com/streamlit/docs/blob/695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd/content/kb/FAQ/where-file-uploader-store-when-deleted.md
```

محدودیت: مستندات رسمی Streamlit بیان می‌کند که داده‌های آپلود شده توسط `st.file_uploader` به صورت یک بافر BytesIO در حافظه RAM نگهداری می‌شوند و این داده‌ها تا اجرای مجدد کل برنامه حفظ می‌شوند. گزارش کاربر نشان می‌دهد هنگام آپلود فایل بسیار بزرگ (~3.5 گیگابایت) مصرف RAM افزایش شدیدی دارد و سرور در نهایت کرش می‌کند. بررسی دقیق مصرف RAM هنگام آپلود فایل می‌تواند تعیین کند که آیا این موضوع به دلیل طراحی داخلی `st.file_uploader` است یا عامل دیگری موجب کرش سرور شده است.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: داده آپلود شده در حافظه RAM نگه داشته می‌شود تا اجرای بعدی کل برنامه، پس افزایش مصرف RAM هنگام آپلود یک فایل بزرگ منطقی است.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.
next_step: مصرف دقیق حافظه RAM را در هنگام اجرای `st.file_uploader` و آپلود فایل بزرگ با پایش سیستم (مثلاً با ابزارهای btop یا مشابه) مورد بررسی قرار دهید تا الگوی افزایش مصرف حافظه مشخص شود.

st.data_editor infer empty column as Multiselect column instead of Text column

### Checklist

- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.data_editor infer empty column as Multiselect column instead of Text column. As a result, text input in a cell of an empty column is stored in a list in the underlying pandas DataFrame. For example, entering `"my value"` results to `["my value"]` in the DataFrame cell. Even explicitly configuring the column as Text column with `st.column_config.TextColumn` does not work. The bug is introduced by the recent 1.52.0 release. I believe it's due to this change:
```
if column_data_kind in (ColumnDataKind.LIST, ColumnDataKind.EMPTY):
            return list(value) if is_list_like(value) else [value]  # ty: ignore 
```
From this merged PR:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/12935/files

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

df = pd.DataFrame([{'a': None}])

modified_df = st.data_editor(df)

print(modified_df)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

محدودیت: در شواهد ارسالی، گزارش شده که پس از نسخه 1.52.0، ستون‌های خالی به اشتباه به صورت ستون چند انتخابی (لیستی) شناسایی می‌شوند. همچنین، کاربر اشاره کرده که حتی تعیین صریح ستون متنی توسط `st.column_config.TextColumn` نیز تاثیری نداشته است. برای تفکیک اینکه آیا مشکل ناشی از تغییر در داخلی `st.data_editor` است یا نحوه استفاده کاربر، لازم است کد مربوط به پیکربندی ستون‌ها دیده شود. بدون این اطلاعات، نمی‌توان به طور قطعی پاسخ داد.

st.data_editor infer empty column as Multiselect column instead of Text column

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.data_editor infer empty column as Multiselect column instead of Text column. As a result, text input in a cell of an empty column is stored in a list in the underlying pandas DataFrame. For example, entering `"my value"` results to `["my value"]` in the DataFrame cell. Even explicitly configuring the column as Text column with `st.column_config.TextColumn` does not work. The bug is introduced by the recent 1.52.0 release. I believe it's due to this change:
```
if column_data_kind in (ColumnDataKind.LIST, ColumnDataKind.EMPTY):
            return list(value) if is_list_like(value) else [value]  # ty: ignore 
```
From this merged PR:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/12935/files

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

df = pd.DataFrame([{'a': None}])

modified_df = st.data_editor(df)

print(modified_df)
```

_No response_

Input "text" should set the text in the DataFrame cell, not a list. 

### Current Behavior

```python
# comp.py

import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import streamlit as st

st_comp_get_cookies = st.components.v2.component(
    "component_bidi_drop_bug.get_cookies",
    js="""
    export default function(component){
        const { data, setTriggerValue } = component;
        console.log("Comp Instantiated: " + data._);
        // More advanced logic here
        const retObj = document.cookie;
        console.log("cookie-getter:", retObj);
        if(retObj !== undefined) setTriggerValue("get_cookies", retObj);
    }
    """,
    isolate_styles=False,
)

def _frame_gen(frame, skip=0):
    while frame:
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"
```

streamlit v 1.55

I'm trying to migrate our custom js widgets from v1 component api to the non-iframe v2 api.
It seems far more powerful, and seems like it'll cut boilerplate.
In our style, we have accumulated over the years a collection of js/client side running code, that doesn't particularly need/have an html or user-interfacing component.

I think I've noticed an issue, where values are getting returned from the js frontend (as seen by console.log msgs), but the streamlit backend logs see those msgs as dropped. I'm still getting the hang of the runtime behaviors of this new component api, to figure out how to update our v1 components, so I've been trying to test it. If this is not the expected or correct usage, I'm all ears, but I'm working my best from the online docs + repo src implementation. 

This is our current design / usage analysis of the v2 api:
- We declare/write a st.components.v2.component(...) object in a helper file, that will not be modified, with a unique name
- The js string includes all helper functions, and an `export default function(component: FrontendRendererArgs)`
- This default function is the per-widget-instantiation, and only run once (see below)
- It sets up callbacks or such on html elements
- If the component is called with a `key`, then all setTriggerValue and setStateValue items populate session_state
- Without an explicit `key`, setTriggerValue won't populate session_state, but the rest of the python arguments (data) are used to calculate a unique frontend key
- No two component instances therefore can have the exact same args (data)
- If the args to the component don't change, the widget object stays created, and is not re-instantiated
- If the rest of the args (data) to the component change, without a `key`, the old widget is discarded, and a new component is instantiated

Our goal is to have high-level code that uses caching & post processing of raw lower-level data call these low-level components as needed. But if the components are called, I expect them to behave consistently. 

In this particular example, the js component does (for example!!!) a failproof cookies query on instantiation and returns it via setTriggerValue.
```js
export default function (component){  component.setTriggerValue("get_cookies", document.cookie); }
```
We wrap that `st_comp_get_cookies: st.components.v2.component` in a helper function.
```python
def get_raw_cookies():
    obj = st_comp_get_cookies(data={"_": unique_line_time()})
```
If we feed `data` a value that's unique to the line (line traceback stack), the multiple calls of the widget will be unique even if fed the same other args. It would create a new component when there's a new/unique call (args or location), otherwise only instantiated once.
If we feed `data` a value that's unique in time, then every call is a new widget instance, and the js default function runs each time.

In the v1 api, when the app first loaded, the components wouldn't always respond right away. So I'd check if the returned value was empty or not.
```python
# get_raw_cookies()
if not isisntance(obj, dict) or "get_cookies" not in obj:
    # Very first run, component mightn't be ready
    time.sleep(initial_setup_sleep)
    st.rerun()
print(f"{obj["get_cookies"]=}")
```

Given the above files, with more logging added, I noticed a very strange behavior. (This is just a heavily reduced version of our real prod code; and I only chose documents.cookies because it _can't fail_).
In the browser console, everytime the page reloaded (hard reload F5, or soft rerun from some other input), the console logged the new widget instance, the cookie fetch, and that succeeded.
But in the python logs, sometimes it worked, sometimes it did not. 
With the "rerun if fail" check, if this was the only indeterminite execution, it'd work quickly enough, and then the rest of the code would execute.
But with multiple components doing this, it suddenly became impossible for both to work at the same time.
```python
get_raw_cookies() # Sometimes reruns, ok
get_raw_cookies() # Always reruns, when the above finally works
st.header("This never runs")
assert False
```

Sorry if this was rather long winded, but I'm either uncertain I'm understanding the runtime behaviors correctly, trying not to misrepresent our goals, possibly oblivious to a better v2 design, or just unaware of what to reasonably expect from this as for behavior.


### Steps To Reproduce

2. docker compose up (or, it's _really just_ python 3.10 and streamlit 1.55 in the env, nothing else)
3. Open browser to streamlit instance
4. Compare the browser logs, the python logs, and how the page doesn't load

### Expected Behavior

I expect at app start the component to fail, but afterwards I'd expect each new component creation to successfully be created, successfully transmit setState/TriggerValue back to the component, and get returned by the component, before the backend continues on. (Consistency / Determinism). (Otherwise, we'd design differently)

### Current Behavior

I've tried variations of the above files, such as adding more sleeps on python side, but the js side seems to be sending the values back, and the python side seems to inconsistently receive them. The first component ~1/2 the time, and the second always fails when the first doesn't.

st.tabs switches back to the first tab if an element is added or removed before the tabs

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Tabs should (and usually do) save their state between reruns so that if I adjust a widget inside a tab, that same tab stays visible.
However, if the rerun adds/removes a widget _above_ the tabs' declaration, the tab state is reset to the first tab no matter which tab was visible when the above-the-tabs widget was added/removed.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

if "enabled" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled:
    st.button("Hi there!")

a, b = st.tabs(["Tab 1", "Tab 2"])

if "enabled_safe" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled_safe:
    st.button("Phew, safe!")

with a:
    st.write("Hello, world!")

with b:
    message = """Toggling the first switch will cause a button to
appear or disappear above the tabs. This causes the tabs to
reset to the first tab, incorrectly, in my opinion.

Toggling the second (safe) switch causes the button to appear
or disappear below the tabs, which preserves the tab state (correctly)."""
    st.write(message)
    enabled = st.toggle("Display it!", key="enabled")
    enabled_safe = st.toggle("This one's safe", key="enabled_safe")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch the provided code example
2. Open Tab 2 to reveal the toggles
3. Toggle the "Display it!" switch which will cause a new button to appear above the tabs
4. The tab will reset to Tab 1

I have experimented with a few different setups and it appears only adding/removing widgets causes this issue.
Simply changing the state of a widget (e.g. the label of a button) does not cause this issue.

### Expected Behavior

I expect that having a new button or other widget appear above a set of tabs
would not change which tab is currently visible.

I believe this is the same issue as #11160 but that issue author never responded.

initial_report:
For deferred download with `st.download_button`, pipe errors to the script thread

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

If you use deferred download with `st.download_button`, there should be a way to catch errors that may be raised by the deferred generation function. Currently, if the funciton encounters an error, a warning message is displayed on the frontend and isn't accessible on the backend.

### Why?

When you use deferred download with `st.download_button`, the function which returns the download runs on its own thread so it won't block the script thread. This has two consequences:
1. There is no script context, so you can't use any Streamlit command, like `st.session_state`. (See #13337).
2. You can't handle errors raised by the deferred download function.

You can put try-catch blocks in your download function to avoid an unhandled error, but you can't really _do_ anything about it because you can't display a custom message or log something in Session State. (Maybe you could hack a solution by writing something to a temporary file on the server, but that doesn't seem ideal.)

### How?

A couple different solutions:
* Have the download button return an error if encountered so it can be caught in the main script.
* Give the download thread some (possibly restricted) script context (like #13337).
* Improve multithreading support more generally, and have some hook at the end of a script run to catch a session's child threads, like the download thread.

### Additional Context

st.tabs switches back to the first tab if an element is added or removed before the tabs

### Summary

Tabs should (and usually do) save their state between reruns so that if I adjust a widget inside a tab, that same tab stays visible.
However, if the rerun adds/removes a widget _above_ the tabs' declaration, the tab state is reset to the first tab no matter which tab was visible when the above-the-tabs widget was added/removed.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

if "enabled" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled:
    st.button("Hi there!")

a, b = st.tabs(["Tab 1", "Tab 2"])

if "enabled_safe" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled_safe:
    st.button("Phew, safe!")

with a:
    st.write("Hello, world!")

with b:
    message = """Toggling the first switch will cause a button to
appear or disappear above the tabs. This causes the tabs to
reset to the first tab, incorrectly, in my opinion.

Toggling the second (safe) switch causes the button to appear
or disappear below the tabs, which preserves the tab state (correctly)."""
    st.write(message)
    enabled = st.toggle("Display it!", key="enabled")
    enabled_safe = st.toggle("This one's safe", key="enabled_safe")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch the provided code example
2. Open Tab 2 to reveal the toggles
3. Toggle the "Display it!" switch which will cause a new button to appear above the tabs
4. The tab will reset to Tab 1

I have experimented with a few different setups and it appears only adding/removing widgets causes this issue.
Simply changing the state of a widget (e.g. the label of a button) does not cause this issue.

### Expected Behavior

I expect that having a new button or other widget appear above a set of tabs
would not change which tab is currently visible.

### Current Behavior

See steps to reproduce.

- Browser: Brave (Chrome) (Brave 1.83.118 / Chromium: 141.0.7390.108)


### Additional Information

I believe this is the same issue as #11160 but that issue author never responded.

initial_report:
For deferred download with `st.download_button`, pipe errors to the script thread

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

If you use deferred download with `st.download_button`, there should be a way to catch errors that may be raised by the deferred generation function. Currently, if the funciton encounters an error, a warning message is displayed on the frontend and isn't accessible on the backend.

### Why?

When you use deferred download with `st.download_button`, the function which returns the download runs on its own thread so it won't block the script thread. This has two consequences:
1. There is no script context, so you can't use any Streamlit command, like `st.session_state`. (See #13337).
2. You can't handle errors raised by the deferred download function.

You can put try-catch blocks in your download function to avoid an unhandled error, but you can't really _do_ anything about it because you can't display a custom message or log something in Session State. (Maybe you could hack a solution by writing something to a temporary file on the server, but that doesn't seem ideal.)

### How?

A couple different solutions:
* Have the download button return an error if encountered so it can be caught in the main script.

initial_report:
st.cache_data on class methods intermittently raises UnserializableReturnValueError

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'X'>: it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
### `repro_model.py`


"""Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file."""

class MyResult:
    def __init__(self, output: str = "", value: int = 0):
        self.output = output
        self.value = value


### `repro_agent.py`


"""
Helper module imported once by repro.py.
Simulates agents/__init__.py — only loaded once, holds a stale class reference
after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher.
"""
import streamlit as st
from repro_model import MyResult  # bound once at import time


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    import time
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return MyResult(output=f"result for {key}", value=42)


### `repro.py` — run with `streamlit run repro.py`


import streamlit as st
import sys
import importlib
import repro_agent  # imported once — simulates agents/__init__.py


st.title("cache_data pickle race condition repro")

if st.button("1) Normal call (works)"):
    try:
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")

if st.button("2) Simulate file-watcher then call (fails, and keeps failing)"):
    # This is exactly what LocalSourcesWatcher.on_path_changed does:
    #   for wm in self._watched_modules.values():
    #       del sys.modules[wm.module_name]
    if "repro_model" in sys.modules:
        del sys.modules["repro_model"]

    # Re-import creates a NEW class object in sys.modules
    importlib.import_module("repro_model")

    # Clear cache so pickle.dumps is attempted again
    repro_agent.get_result.clear()

    try:
        # repro_agent still uses the OLD MyResult class.
        # pickle resolves sys.modules["repro_model"].MyResult → NEW class.
        # OLD is not NEW → PicklingError → UnserializableReturnValueError
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

**Steps:**
1. `streamlit run repro.py`
2. Click **"1) Normal call"** — succeeds.
3. Click **"2) Simulate file-watcher"** — fails with `UnserializableReturnValueError`.
4. Click **"1) Normal call"** again — **also fails**, until Streamlit is restarted.


### Expected Behavior

Step 4 demonstrates persistence: `repro_agent` is never re-imported, so it keeps
using the old class, while `sys.modules` keeps the new one.

Neither step 3 not step 4 should throw the `UnserializableReturnValueError`.

Expected behavior : 

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Current Behavior

`UnserializableReturnValueError` is thrown

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- **Streamlit**: 1.55.0
- **Python**: 3.13.7
- **OS**: Windows 11 / Linux (Kubernetes)
- Occurs more frequently in local dev (active filesystem) than in deployed containers

### Additional Information

> **Disclosure**: This bug report was written by an LLM (Claude) after a deep investigation into a production issue. The root cause analysis, reproduction script, and identified problematic code path are all LLM-generated

## Suggested Fixes

### Option A: Chain the original exception (low-effort, improves DX)

In `_handle_cache_miss`, chain the original exception so users can see the real error:

```python
raise UnserializableReturnValueError(
    return_value=computed_value, func=self._info.func
) from ex  # <-- add "from ex"
```

### Option B: Guard `write_result` against stale class references

Before calling `pickle.dumps()` in `DataCache.write_result`, re-import the module and verify class identity:

```python
import importlib
cls = type(value)
mod = sys.modules.get(cls.__module__)
if mod is not None:
    current_cls = getattr(mod, cls.__qualname__, None)
    if current_cls is not None and current_cls is not cls:
        # Module was reloaded — update the instance's class to the current one
        value.__class__ = current_cls
```

### Option C: Don't delete modules from `sys.modules` preemptively

Instead of deleting all watched modules on every file change, only invalidate the module that actually changed. Or defer the deletion to the start of the next script run rather than doing it immediately from the watcher thread.

## Workaround

Return only pickle-safe primitives (dicts, strings, numbers) from `@st.cache_data` functions, and reconstruct custom objects outside the cache boundary:

```python
@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def _cached_call(key: str) -> dict:
    result = do_expensive_work(key)
    return result.__dict__  # dict is always pickle-safe

def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    return MyResult(**_cached_call(key))
```

بخش منبع:

```text
Where does st.file_uploader store uploaded files and when do they get deleted?
```

نسخهٔ منبع:

```text
695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd
```

متن شاهد:

```text
When you upload a file using [`st.file_uploader`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader), the data are copied to the Streamlit backend via the browser, and contained in a BytesIO buffer in Python memory (i.e. RAM, not disk). The data will persist in RAM until the Streamlit app re-runs from top-to-bottom, which is on each widget interaction. If you need to save the data that was uploaded between runs, then you can [cache](/develop/concepts/architecture/caching) it so that Streamlit persists it across re-runs.
```


محدودیت: بر اساس اسناد رسمی، داده‌های آپلود شده یک فایل در `st.file_uploader` در حافظه RAM قرار می‌گیرند و تا زمان اجرای مجدد کل برنامه از اول به طور کامل نگه داشته می‌شوند. گزارش شما نشان می‌دهد مصرف RAM پس از آپلود باقی می‌ماند حتی پس از بستن تب مرورگر ولی تنها با بستن کل برنامه پاک می‌شود که با مدیریت حافظه توصیف شده همسو نیست. بررسی مصرف حافظه بدون st.rerun() می‌تواند مشخص کند آیا تابع st.rerun() یا دیگر عملیات پس از آپلود منجر به حفظ حافظه می‌شود یا خیر.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: ممکن است فایل آپلود شده پس از ارسال پاک نشود به دلیل نحوه مدیریت حافظه استریم‌لیت باشد.
